I personally don’t mind either or, I just wanna make a decision on this yes, I think that was the idea, to keep it separate as long as we are not 100% sure it won’t delay pectra (much) and once we are closer to actual fork we can decide to have it included or not. ok that is a better reason Execution layer clients have had peer-EIP activations since a while ago, such as Nethermind: ``` "params": { "eip3529Transition": "0x0", "eip3541Transition": "0x0", "eip1153TransitionTimestamp": "0x65F23E01", "eip4788TransitionTimestamp": "0x65F23E01", "eip4844TransitionTimestamp": "0x65F23E01", "eip5656TransitionTimestamp": "0x65F23E01", "eip6780TransitionTimestamp": "0x65F23E01", ``` What structure specifically? We should not force a fork_version change when we can update our spec infra to handle it This will require a more work from us though, in the call when this was agreed I assumed we would just be using `EIP7594_FORK_EPOCH` + `DENEB_VERSION` as this is technically what was done at the interop in that case eip7594_fork_verison needs to be gone from the spec. If clients prefer to treat EIP7594 as a regular fork in the context of consensus forks that's fine. As long as we can commit to `EIP7594_FORK_VERSION` to being equal to the fork_version at `EIP7594_FORK_EPOCH` it's okay with me Right, clients can emulate a hard-fork from `EIP7594_FORK_EPOCH` by making up `EIP7594_FORK_VERSION` internally Hi! Some reasons for pro-fork-epoch: 1. PeerDAS requires nodes upgrade together as much as a hard fork level. Specifically, we want all nodes to switch together at the the specific epoch and deprecate the old blob sidecar subnets simultaneously. 2. PeerDAS may be essential for the blob count bump EIP. Maybe better to delay the decision of `*_ACTIVATION_EPOCH` to the point we have more data of the chance to bump blob count. Because if we do so, we may have to revert back to `_FORK_EPOCH` again. 😅 agree 👍 For CL specs, we just didn't support "non-fork" features for versioning. We currently need an explicit `upgrade_to_eip7594` function somewhere, OR we need to hard-code something in spec builder... (🤢). I can explore it, but I am also thinking about the possibility that we may revert to it due to blob count or network health above. Why do you need a `upgrade_to_eip7594` function? All the code in the fork as of now is networking functions which we don't use in the spec as executable I assume? You could just delete the `specs/_features/eip7594/fork.md` file 😄 or just delete the "Upgrading the state" section

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content:
On the peerdas call, the consensus was to activate peerdas going forward as a hard fork. Keeping 
```
EIP7594_FORK_VERSION
EIP7594_FORK_EPOCH
```

This will be the same as it was on devnet 0. Once devnet-x is very stable, and we have a good idea whether to actually have this activated in the same epoch as pectra, then we can come back to renaming these variables in the spec.

excerpts.author: hsiaowei
excerpts.content:
Hi! Some reasons for pro-fork-epoch:
1. PeerDAS requires nodes upgrade together as much as a hard fork level. Specifically, we want all nodes to switch together at the the specific epoch and deprecate the old blob sidecar subnets simultaneously.
2. PeerDAS may be essential for the blob count bump EIP. Maybe better to delay the decision of `*_ACTIVATION_EPOCH` to the point we have more data of the chance to bump blob count. Because if we do so, we may have to revert back to `_FORK_EPOCH` again. 😅

excerpts.author: hsiaowei
excerpts.content:
agree 👍 

For CL specs, we just didn't support "non-fork" features for versioning. We currently need an explicit `upgrade_to_eip7594` function somewhere, OR we need to hard-code something in spec builder... (🤢). I can explore it, but I am also thinking about the possibility that we may revert to it due to blob count or network health above.
